Lament

/luh-MENT/ — stress on the second syllable · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To lament something is to express deep sadness or regret about it.

Fans around the world lamented the retirement of their favorite player.

Worked Example

When a beloved actor announced her retirement, fans posted videos and articles mourning her departure. Some wept openly; others wrote heartfelt essays. The film industry lamented the loss of one of its finest talents.

'Lament' is more precise than 'regret' or 'mourn' here because it captures the act of publicly, formally expressing grief or sorrow about something. It's not just feeling sad—the fans are actively voicing their sadness in multiple ways. Lament describes that shared, expressed sorrow.

How Lament Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

regret

regret: quietly wishing something had not happened

mourn

mourn: to grieve a death or serious loss

bemoan

bemoan: to complain unhappily about something out loud

Antonyms

celebrate

celebrate: to mark a happy event with joy

rejoice

rejoice: to feel or show great delight

How Strong Is It? — regret → bemoan → lament → wail

regret vs. lament

regret vs. lament: Regret is weaker than lament — regret is a private wish that things had gone differently, while to lament is to give that sorrow a full, open voice.

bemoan vs. lament

bemoan vs. lament: Bemoan is weaker than lament; bemoaning is grumbling unhappily about a problem, while lamenting pours out deep, heartfelt grief.

wail vs. lament

wail vs. lament: Wail is stronger and rawer than lament — a lament can be dignified words of sorrow, but wailing is loud, uncontrolled crying that words can no longer manage.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — lament

Root — lament: a wailing, moaning, weeping (from lamentum) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Lament comes whole from Latin lamentum, 'a wailing or weeping cry' — so to lament something is literally to give your grief a voice.

Use the root in a new word: lamentable

Use the root in a new word: lamentable: The state of the flooded library was lamentable — a sight so sad that everyone who saw it wanted to lament its ruin.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Lament is serious and often literary—the formal expression of deep sadness or regret. Use it when someone voices or publicly expresses sorrow. For silent feeling or mild complaint, 'regret,' 'miss,' or 'bemoan' work better.
